June 15 now has two posts, because the cathedral plainly overpowered the day and demanded its own chamber. Sensible. The focused cathedral post is here: [Otranto Cathedral: Basilica of the Annunciation and the Tree of Life](otranto-cathedral-tree-of-life.qmd).

This post keeps the rest of the day: Otranto as Adriatic harbor, lunch by the water, and the evening coastal run to **Punta Palascia / Cape Otranto** and **Porto Badisco**.

The itinerary had Otranto as an ancient Adriatic port town: Greek Hydrus, Roman port, a place facing the Balkans and Greece, with Albania visible across the water on a clear day. That orientation mattered all day. Otranto does not feel like an endpoint so much as one side of a crossing.

Lunch was in the harbor overlooking the Adriatic: fresh vegetables, sea bream, a light torte, and lots of fruit. It sounds exactly right for the place — water in front of you, clean food, and nothing heavy enough to deaden the afternoon.

The evening plan added one more coastal turn. At **17:00**, the group met in the courtyard for pickup. The first stop was **Il Faro** at **Punta Palascia / Cape Otranto**, the easternmost point of Italy; the second was **Porto Badisco**, for bar food, drinks, fun friends, and great sea views. Return to **Masseria dei Monaci** was scheduled for **19:30**.

![Il Faro at Punta Palascia / Cape Otranto, the easternmost point of Italy, looking out over the Adriatic.](images/punta-palascia-lighthouse-easternmost-italy.jpeg){fig-alt="A white lighthouse complex at Punta Palascia on a rocky coastal slope above the Adriatic Sea, with low vegetation, stone walls, and hazy blue water beyond."}

It makes a good closing shape for the day: cathedral floor in the morning, harbor lunch at midday, and then lighthouse, inlet, drinks, and sea views before returning home.
